Servile
sŭr´vĭl
adj. (of or belonging to a servant; laborious; Hebrew 'abodah, work of a bondman)
Latin servilis, of a slave, from servus. In Leviticus 23 it defines what may not be done on a holy convocation: servile work, the labour of a bondservant.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Servile occurs in the KJV almost entirely in one formula, and that formula structures Israel's calendar. Of unleavened bread: “In the first day ye shall have an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein” (Lev 23:7), and of the seventh day of the feast, “in the seventh day is an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein” (Lev 23:8). Of the feast of weeks: “And ye shall proclaim on the selfsame day, that it may be an holy convocation unto you: ye shall do no servile work therein: it shall be a statute for ever in all your dwellings throughout your generations” (Lev 23:21). Of the feast of trumpets: “Ye shall do no servile work therein: but ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD” (Lev 23:25). And of tabernacles: “On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein” (Lev 23:35). The phrase is not a general ban on effort — the same days require offerings, and the priests worked hardest of all. It forbids the labour of a bondman, the work a slave does because he must.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines servile as pertaining to a servant or slave; slavish; dependent; and, of labour, mean, base, or such as is performed by servants.

expand to see more

SERVILE, a. Pertaining to a servant or slave; slavish; mean.

2. Dependent; held in subjection; not free.

3. Cringing; fawning; meanly submissive.

SERVITUDE, n. The condition of a slave; the state of involuntary subjection to a master.

Key Scripture

Lev 23:7 — "In the first day ye shall have an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein."

Lev 23:21 — "And ye shall proclaim on the selfsame day, that it may be an holy convocation unto you: ye shall do no servile work therein: it shall be a statute for ever in all your dwellings throughout your generations."

Lev 23:25 — "Ye shall do no servile work therein: but ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD."

Lev 23:35 — "On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein."

Modern Corruption

Rest is treated as recovery time for more production, while Leviticus forbids the labour of a bondman on the LORD's days and commands worship in its place.

expand to see more

The precision of the phrase is the point. Leviticus does not say do no work on these days; it says do no servile work, the labour of a bondservant. The same chapters command offerings made by fire, which is real labour, and the priests were busiest on the holy convocations. What is forbidden is the work a man does under compulsion, for his living, as a slave does — and the reason is stated in Deuteronomy 5:15: remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt.

This is the standing correction to a productivity culture that has learned to justify rest only as an input to more output. Israel's calendar interrupted the harvest itself; the feast of weeks fell in the middle of the grain, and the LORD required them to stop and assemble. A day off taken to be a better worker on Monday is not what Leviticus commands. The convocation is the point, and the ceasing is what makes room for it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mele'keth 'abodah, work of service or servile work; from 'abodah (H5656), labour, bondage — the same root as 'ebed, servant; miqra' qodesh, holy convocation.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'abodah (H5656) — service, labour, bondage; the servile work forbidden.

Hebrew 'ebed (H5650) — servant, bondman; the same root, and Israel's memory of Egypt.

Hebrew mela'kah (H4399) — work, occupation; paired with 'abodah in the formula.

Hebrew miqra' qodesh — holy convocation; the positive command of the same verses.

Hebrew shabbathon (H7677) — a sabbath of rest; the character of the day.

Usage

"“Ye shall do no servile work therein” — five times in one chapter."

"“But ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD” — ceasing is not idleness."

"“A statute for ever in all your dwellings throughout your generations” — not a seasonal favour."
